stories.headline: Ukraine says SpaceX capped military Starlink speeds without warning, disrupting drone missions

key_facts.fact: Ukrainian presidential adviser Serhiy Beskrestnov said SpaceX overnight on Oct 13-14 imposed speed restrictions on Starlink terminals in motion, applying to the Starshield 'military service package' and capping it at 100 mph (160 km/h).
key_facts.excerpt: I confirm that (Starlink owner) SpaceX implemented speed restrictions on Starlink terminals while in motion last night. Currently, the restriction applies to the StarShield 'military service package' and limits speed to 100 miles per hour (160 kilometers per hour)

key_facts.fact: Beskrestnov said Ukraine's defence forces received no warning and several missions were disrupted, adding the move 'cannot be a coincidence' and is linked to the political situation.
key_facts.excerpt: "Our defence forces did not receive a warning about this limitation, and this led to the disruption of several missions," presidential adviser Serhiy Beskrestnov wrote on Telegram.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's 7th Rapid Reaction Corps told Reuters connections dropped for 10-20 seconds at speeds of just 110-120 km/h, forcing units to cancel some missions.
key_facts.excerpt: during flights, the connection could drop for 10–20 seconds at speeds of just 110–120 km/h. The drones kept moving, but these interruptions made them harder to control

key_facts.fact: Starlink guides Ukraine's mid-range strike drones and the interceptor drones it uses against Russia's new jet-powered attack drones.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine relies on Starlink for several military applications including operating its mid-strike campaign in Russian-occupied Ukraine, as well as interceptor drones that defend against Russia's new jet-powered attack drones.

key_facts.fact: A Ukrainian drone-unit commander told POLITICO the restrictions brought all medium-range strike operations to a complete halt; a defence ministry official said problems occur at 72-161 km/h depending on vehicle and unit.
key_facts.excerpt: The restrictions have brought "all medium-range strike operations to a complete halt," the officer said ... the problems occur at speeds varying from 72 kph to 161 kph, "depending on the specific vehicle and unit."

key_facts.fact: The limits come as Trump pressures Kyiv to stop hitting Russian oil refineries; the WSJ reports Trump has also blamed Zelensky for continuing the war and called for his removal.
key_facts.excerpt: The limits on Starlink ... come as President Trump piles pressure on Ukraine, demanding that it stop hitting Russian oil refineries, blaming President Volodymyr Zelensky for continuing the war and calling for his removal.

key_facts.fact: On Oct 13 Zelensky told NPR the Trump administration warned it could cut off intelligence-sharing unless Ukraine stops long-range drone strikes on Russian refineries; Trump said the US is still sharing intel.
key_facts.excerpt: The Trump administration warned it could cut off intelligence-sharing with Ukraine unless Ukrainian forces stop long-range drone strikes on oil refineries inside Russia, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told NPR.

stories.headline: Houthi strike hits Saudi Aramco headquarters in Dhahran; Houthis vow more attacks on oil sites

key_facts.fact: Houthi rebels hit Saudi Aramco's headquarters in Dhahran in an overnight strike on Oct 13, damaging the offices of the company's chief executive and other top officials, two regional officials told AP.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran-backed Houthi rebels hit the headquarters of the Saudi state-owned oil company Aramco in an overnight strike, two regional officials said Wednesday, damaging the offices of the firm's chief executive and other top officials.

key_facts.fact: The Saudi energy ministry said the strike caused a 'limited fire', but three people with knowledge of the matter told Reuters the fire spread across several floors.
key_facts.excerpt: Tuesday night's attack on Saudi Aramco's base in the eastern city of Dhahran caused a fire that spread across several floors, three people with knowledge of the matter told Reuters. The Saudi energy ministry had said the strike caused a limited fire.

key_facts.fact: Debris from two intercepted Houthi cruise missiles wounded four people in Riyadh and damaged 15 homes, Saudi civil defence said.
key_facts.excerpt: Saudi's civil defence agency separately said on Wednesday that debris from two intercepted Houthi missiles wounded four people in the capital Riyadh, and that 15 homes were damaged.

key_facts.fact: The Saudi-led coalition struck Houthi energy sites in Yemen, including the Al Sabahah fuel station in Sanaa and fuel-loading piers at Hodeidah port, after issuing an evacuation order.
key_facts.excerpt: The Saudi-led coalition struck energy sites in Houthi-held Yemen, including a fuel station in Sanaa and loading piers at the Red Sea port of Hodeidah.

key_facts.fact: On Oct 14 the Houthis vowed to keep attacking Saudi airports and oil facilities and urged shipping companies and workers to evacuate them; the coalition said it intercepted a ballistic missile fired at Riyadh.
key_facts.excerpt: Yemen's Houthis vowed on Wednesday to press on with attacks on airports and oil facilities in Saudi Arabia ... The Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted a ballistic missile fired by the Houthis towards Riyadh on Wednesday

key_facts.fact: Trump wrote on Truth Social that the Houthis are 'behaving very badly', probably at Iran's behest, and are 'purposefully trying to drive up Oil Prices, probably prior to the US elections'; the Houthis warned they would target US interests if Washington intervenes.
key_facts.excerpt: "...hitting Saudi Arabia, and purposefully trying to drive up Oil Prices, probably prior to the US elections — not nice." The Houthis warned the US against intervention

key_facts.fact: A weekend Houthi attack on Riyadh's King Khalid international airport killed 14 people and wounded more than 300, per Al Jazeera's updated toll.
key_facts.excerpt: Houthi attacks on Riyadh's King Khalid international airport over the weekend killed 14 people and wounded more than 300 others.

stories.headline: US inflation rises to 3.7% in September as gasoline jumps 9.1%, reviving Fed hike bets

key_facts.fact: The US consumer price index rose 0.6% in September and 3.7% from a year earlier, up from 3.4% in August, the BLS reported on Oct 14.
key_facts.excerpt: The consumer price index showed annual inflation of 3.7% in September after rising 0.6% for the month, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Wednesday.

key_facts.fact: Economists surveyed by Dow Jones had expected 0.6% monthly and 3.6% annual; core CPI rose 0.3% on the month and 2.6% on the year versus estimates of 0.2% and 2.5%.
key_facts.excerpt: Economists surveyed by Dow Jones expected respective gains of 0.6% and 3.6%. ... core CPI rose 0.3% for the month and was up 2.6% on an annual basis, compared with respective estimates for 0.2% and 2.5%.

key_facts.fact: Gasoline rose 9.1% in the month and accounted for about half the headline gain; the energy index jumped 5.2%, and over 12 months gas is up 34.2% and fuel oil 74.2%.
key_facts.excerpt: The energy index jumped 5.2% ... Gasoline prices soared 9.1%, accounting for about half the gain in headline CPI ... Over the past year, gas has posted a 34.2% rise while fuel oil has roared higher by 74.2%.

key_facts.fact: The 0.6% monthly increase was the biggest gain in five months, AP reported, weeks before midterm elections focused on affordability.
key_facts.excerpt: On a monthly basis, costs jumped 0.6% from August to September, the biggest gain in five months

key_facts.fact: The report comes two weeks before the FOMC's Oct 28 decision; the Fed hiked rates by a quarter point last month.
key_facts.excerpt: The data from the BLS comes two weeks before the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) will decide whether to raise interest rates again. The FOMC last month hiked rates by a quarter point

key_facts.fact: Reuters said the surge in gasoline costs put an interest-rate increase later this month back on the radar.
key_facts.excerpt: US consumer prices accelerated in September with a surge in gasoline costs putting an interest rate increase later this month back on the radar.

stories.headline: US charges 14 and dismantles 40+ Texas laptop farms in North Korean IT worker crackdown

key_facts.fact: The Justice Department on Oct 13 announced coordinated actions against North Korean remote IT worker schemes affecting more than 70 US companies.
key_facts.excerpt: Justice Department Announces Coordinated Actions to Combat North Korean Remote IT Worker Schemes Affecting More than 70 U.S. Companies

key_facts.fact: An indictment unsealed in the Northern District of Ohio charges 14 people, including US citizens Michael James Bostelle and Juan Cecilio Pena Carrillo (both arrested) and 10 China-based defendants, over a scheme that collected about $3 million in pay.
key_facts.excerpt: Federal authorities have charged 14 people ... An indictment unsealed in the Northern District of Ohio charges two U.S. citizens, Michael James Bostelle of Pennsylvania and Juan Cecilio Pena Carrillo of Texas. It alleges the two Americans, along with 10 others located in China, held remote jobs at more than 70 companies from 2019 through 2025 using stolen or fabricated identities, and collected about $3 million in pay.

key_facts.fact: In Operation Lonestar Roundup, the FBI searched more than 40 Texas residences and seized 187 laptops and other devices used as laptop farms.
key_facts.excerpt: The FBI searched more than 40 Texas residences and seized 187 laptops and other devices used to help North Korean operatives obtain remote jobs at U.S. companies under false identities

key_facts.fact: CrowdStrike, which tracks the network as Famous Chollima, provided intelligence to the FBI; targeted organizations included aerospace, energy, defense engineering and government technology firms.
key_facts.excerpt: CrowdStrike tracks the network under the moniker Famous Chollima ... Organizations identified in the disrupted operations included businesses in aerospace, energy, financial services, health care, cybersecurity, defense engineering and government technology

key_facts.fact: FBI cyber division head Brett Leatherman said every such job funds North Korea's nuclear and ballistic missile programs, calling the action an early example of the FBI's new cyber strategy of closer work with private firms.
key_facts.excerpt: "Every one of these jobs is funding a stream for a nuclear and ballistic missiles program obtained with the stolen identity of an American and the trust of an American employer."

key_facts.fact: Nearly 30 laptop farms across 16 states were raided by US law enforcement last year.
key_facts.excerpt: Nearly 30 laptop farms across 16 states were raided last year by U.S. law enforcement.

stories.headline: Trump says Taiwan will buy 30% of Alaska LNG output and invest $4.4B; Taipei confirms plan

key_facts.fact: At a campaign rally in Wasilla, Alaska on Oct 13, Trump said Taiwan agreed to buy 30% of the gas from the planned Alaska LNG pipeline for 20 years and invest $4.4 billion, on top of $50 billion he said South Korea committed.
key_facts.excerpt: Speaking at a campaign rally in Wasilla, Alaska, Trump said Taiwan will invest $4.4 billion into the project on top of $50 billion already committed by South Korea.

key_facts.fact: Taiwan's Economic Affairs Ministry said on Oct 14 it plans to buy 6 million metric tons of LNG a year from the project once extraction starts and could invest up to $4.4 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Taiwan plans to buy 6 million metric tons (6.6 million U.S. tons) of liquefied natural gas annually from a U.S. project once extraction starts and could invest up to $4.4 billion in it, its Economic Affairs Ministry said Wednesday

key_facts.fact: Taiwan's ministry said Alaska LNG could enter its domestic gas supply as early as 2032 if the project proceeds on schedule.
key_facts.excerpt: If the project proceeds as scheduled, it is expected to be incorporated into Taiwan's domestic gas supply as early as 2032.

key_facts.fact: The 30% share and 20-year term match a nonbinding March 2025 letter of intent from Taiwan's state-owned CPC Corp; neither Trump nor Commerce Secretary Lutnick said whether an agreement had been signed.
key_facts.excerpt: The share and term match a nonbinding letter of intent that Taiwan's state-owned CPC Corporation signed with the Alaska Gasline Development Corporation on March 20, 2025 ... Neither man said whether an agreement had been signed.

key_facts.fact: CNBC noted the terms were not immediately clear and that South Korea's participation in the $50 billion project remains uncertain despite Trump's claims.
key_facts.excerpt: Trump's remarks come amid uncertainty over South Korea's participation in the $50 billion Alaska LNG project, despite his repeated claims that Seoul had agreed to join.

stories.headline: Netflix cuts about 6% of staff, roughly 1,000 jobs, its biggest layoffs since 2022

key_facts.fact: Netflix is cutting 6% of its staff, roughly 1,000 positions globally, its biggest round of layoffs since 2022, as it struggles with slowing growth and customer engagement.
key_facts.excerpt: Netflix is cutting 6% of its staff, or roughly 1,000 positions globally, its biggest round of layoffs since 2022, as it struggles with slowing growth and customer engagement.

key_facts.fact: Co-CEOs Greg Peters and Ted Sarandos told employees in an Oct 14 email that the bulk of the cuts fall on product, tech, legal and HR teams.
key_facts.excerpt: Co-Chief Executives Greg Peters and Ted Sarandos said in an email to employees Wednesday morning that the bulk of the cuts would be in the streaming giant's product, tech, legal and human-resources teams.

key_facts.fact: The memo said the business is 'strong and growing' and the company remains on track to deliver its full-year forecast while continuing to invest 'aggressively in high-impact areas'.
key_facts.excerpt: "Our business is strong and growing, and we remain on track to deliver our full-year forecast," Sarandos and Peters said. "We'll continue to invest aggressively in high-impact areas..."

key_facts.fact: Sarandos said last month at the Bloomberg Screentime summit that Netflix was 'not growing as fast as I want us to'; the company reports results on Oct 20.
key_facts.excerpt: Last month, Netflix's co-chief executive, Ted Sarandos, told the Bloomberg Screentime summit that the company was "not growing as fast as I want us to". ... The streaming service is due [to] report its latest results on 20 October.

key_facts.fact: The co-CEOs wrote that delivering on the mission 'requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritize our people and resources'.
key_facts.excerpt: Netflix cuts about 6% of staff. Sarandos and Peters tell staffers: "Our mission—to entertain the world—is ambitious, and delivering on it requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritize our people and resources."

stories.headline: Zealand Pharma signs up-to-$1.2B deal with Generate Biomedicines for AI-designed obesity drugs

key_facts.fact: Zealand Pharma and Generate Biomedicines on Oct 13 announced a collaboration to design multispecific protein therapeutics for obesity and other metabolic diseases.
key_facts.excerpt: Generate Biomedicines Inc. (Nasdaq: GENB) ("Generate") today announced a multi-target strategic collaboration with Zealand Pharma A/S (Nasdaq: ZEAL) ... to design and develop multispecific protein therapeutics for obesity and other metabolic diseases

key_facts.fact: Generate receives $30 million upfront and up to $35 million in early preclinical milestones, and is eligible for nearly $1.2 billion in total milestones plus tiered royalties for two initial programs, with an option for a third.
key_facts.excerpt: For the two initial programs, Generate will receive $30 million upfront and up to $35 million in early preclinical milestones, and is eligible for total milestones of nearly $1.2 billion

key_facts.fact: Generate will lead research through lead-candidate selection; Zealand will handle clinical development, regulatory submissions and worldwide commercialization.
key_facts.excerpt: Under the agreement, Generate will lead research through candidate selection, while Zealand will handle clinical development, regulatory submissions and worldwide commercialization.

key_facts.fact: Generate's shares rose about 5% in extended trading after the announcement; the Flagship Pioneering-backed company went public earlier this year.
key_facts.excerpt: Generate's shares were up about 5% in extended trading. ... Generate, a Flagship Pioneering-backed biotechnology company that went public earlier this year

key_facts.fact: The agreement broadens Zealand's drug modalities beyond peptides and extends Generate's platform into obesity and metabolic disease.
key_facts.excerpt: The agreement will broaden Zealand Pharma's modality capabilities beyond peptides while extending The Generate Platform into obesity and other metabolic diseases
